title: Energy levels and spectra; Black-body radiation; Stellar luminosity, brightness and distance; Electromagnetic spectrum
source: Questions copied unchanged from the mission-lesson scripts for Eduqas A-level Physics (status of the source: mission-lesson scripts of Oct-Nov 2026 (reviewed by AI reviewers; not signed off by a person)). Terms and clues: Q02-uk1#t4 term and clue written for the game; Q02-uk1#t2 term and clue written for the game; Q02-uk1#t1 term and clue written for the game; T04-1#t1 term and clue written for the game. Questions: A01-1#N.3b, Q02-uk1#N.10, T04-1#N.3, W02-1#N.2, A01-1#N.12a, T04-1#N.8, W02-1#N.14, T04-1#N.10.

assemble.prompt: Match each term to its definition.

items.label: Emission lines
items.clue: Bright features given out by an excited gas at only its own wavelengths.

items.label: Continuous spectrum
items.clue: Light containing all wavelengths, given out by a star's hot, dense surface.

items.label: Discharge tube
items.clue: Low-pressure gas with a high p.d. across it, used to make a gas emit its bright lines.

items.label: Black body
items.clue: Ideal object that absorbs perfectly and emits as well as is possible at its temperature.

questions.stem: A star has 40 times the Sun's luminosity and is 25 ly from the Earth. Take the Sun's luminosity = 3.83 × 10²⁶ W and 1 ly = 9.46 × 10¹⁵ m. What is the intensity of the star's light at the Earth?

options.text: 2.0 × 10²⁴ W m⁻²

questions.stem: A cool cloud of gas lies in front of a hot star, and the star's spectrum seen through the cloud has dark lines. A second telescope views the same cloud from the side, against dark sky, with no star behind it. What does the second telescope see?

options.text: The same dark lines on a continuous band.
A continuous band with no lines.
Nothing at all: the gas absorbs light but does not emit it.
Bright lines at the same wavelengths as the dark lines.

questions.explanation: The atoms re-emit the absorbed photons in all directions. From the side, only those wavelengths arrive: bright lines on a dark background, at the dark lines' wavelengths.

questions.stem: Predict first. A black body is heated to a higher temperature. How does its emission spectrum change?

options.text: It emits more at every wavelength, and the peak moves to a longer wavelength.
It emits more at every wavelength, and its peak moves to a shorter wavelength.
Its peak moves to shorter wavelengths, so it emits less at long wavelengths.
It emits only one wavelength, λ_max, which gets shorter as it gets hotter.

questions.stem: Predict first. Which statement describes the nature of electromagnetic waves?

options.text: Oscillations of the particles of the medium they travel through, so they cannot cross a vacuum
Oscillating electric and magnetic fields that travel faster in a vacuum the higher their frequency
Streams of tiny charged particles given out by the source, which can travel through a vacuum
Oscillating electric and magnetic fields, perpendicular to each other and to the direction of travel

questions.stem: At the Earth, the intensity of star A's light is 4 times that of star B's. Star B is 3 times as far from the Earth as star A. What is the ratio (luminosity of A) ÷ (luminosity of B)?
questions.explanation: L = 4πd² × (power per square metre), so L_A/L_B = 4 × (1/3)² = 4/9 = 0.44: B is the more luminous star.

questions.stem: A small metal sphere of radius 5.0 cm is heated to 527 °C. Treat it as a black body and take σ = 5.67 × 10⁻⁸ W m⁻² K⁻⁴. What power does the sphere emit as thermal radiation?
In a vacuum, the microwaves in a speed camera have a wavelength of 3.0 cm, and the light from a yellow lamp has a wavelength of 600 nm. How do their frequencies compare?

options.text: The microwave frequency is 5 × 10⁴ times the light frequency, since f rises with λ.
They are equal, because both waves travel at the same speed, c, in a vacuum.
The light frequency is 5 × 10⁴ times the microwave frequency, since f = c/λ.
The light frequency is higher, because light travels faster than microwaves.

questions.explanation: Same c for both, so f ∝ 1/λ. Ratio = (3.0 × 10⁻² m)/(600 × 10⁻⁹ m) = 5 × 10⁴: the light's frequency is that many times higher.

questions.stem: A red giant has a luminosity of 100 L⊙ and a surface temperature of 4000 K. A white dwarf has a luminosity of 0.010 L⊙ and a surface temperature of 16 000 K. Both are modelled as black bodies. What is (radius of the red giant)/(radius of the white dwarf)?
